questions.q: What should a consultant do FIRST when designing expense policy for a new client with no existing system?
options: Immediately open Oracle Fusion Expenses setup screens and start building templates
Copy another client's policy exactly, regardless of differences
Issue corporate cards to every employee immediately
Conduct discovery: who travels, what's historically gone wrong, and the company's risk tolerance
questions.explain: Policy design should start with discovery questions about travel patterns, past problems, and risk tolerance, before any Oracle configuration begins.

questions.q: In the Harrowgate example, what were the two specific pain points the controller named?
options: Late payroll and incorrect tax withholding
Fuel card misuse and unsubstantiated client meals
Too many approved vacation days
Incorrect General Ledger account numbering
questions.explain: The controller specifically named fuel card misuse and unsubstantiated client meals as the recurring complaints from manual review.

questions.q: Why did the Harrowgate policy design put Client Entertainment under 100% audit rather than spreading audit effort evenly across all expense types?
options: Because Client Entertainment was a specifically named risk area, so audit effort should concentrate there rather than being wasted evenly on low-risk spend
Because 100% audit of everything is always required by Oracle
Because Client Entertainment expenses are the cheapest category
Because Harrowgate has no sales employees
questions.explain: Audit intensity should follow actual discovered risk; spreading effort evenly wastes reviewer time on categories discovery never flagged as problematic.

questions.q: Why does the lesson emphasize that policy design is 'a business conversation, not a technical one'?
options: Because Oracle configuration is actually impossible to complete
Because business conversations replace the need for any Oracle setup
Because the hard part is getting stakeholders to agree on defensible numbers (like a meal cap), not the technical setup once decisions are made
Because technical configuration always takes longer than stakeholder discussions
questions.explain: Once policy numbers and decisions are agreed upon, building them in Oracle is comparatively straightforward; the harder work is the business negotiation beforehand.

questions.q: Why does the Harrowgate example note that the fleet fuel card program must not be confused with a corporate card program for traveling employees?
options: Because they are actually the exact same system
Because the fuel card is handled outside Expenses through fleet management, while a corporate card program is specifically an Expenses/travel concept
Because fuel cards are illegal for trucking companies
Because corporate cards can only be issued to drivers
questions.explain: The fleet fuel card program for drivers is a separate system outside Expenses, distinct from a corporate card program issued to traveling employees.
